issues.title: New vectorElemMinSize recursion makes nested-vector decode cost cubic in depth
issues.verdictReason: Traced vectorElemMinSize (marshal.go:1125) and isVectorVariableLengthType (marshal.go:1181): each level of vectorElemMinSize's own recursion re-runs isVectorVariableLengthType's full descent to the bottom, giving Θ(depth²) per call; a counted-call probe against depth 10/20/40/80 nested vectors measured 66/231/861/3321 calls, matching the quadratic growth. Since unmarshalVector calls vectorElemMinSize once per nesting level during an actual decode, total cost across a depth-d decode is Θ(d³), confirming the claim.
issues.scopeReason: vectorElemMinSize is new code added by this PR; the quadratic/cubic blowup did not exist before it.

reportedAs.code-review-ad: Recursive sizing causes cubic (Θ(d³)) decoding work for nested vectors

reportedAsByRun.codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17/tidepool: marshal.go:1130 recursively classifies each remaining subtype then repeats classification while recursively calculating its minimum, making classification Θ(d), minimum calculation Θ(d²), and decoding nested singleton vectors Θ(d³) versus Θ(d²) at base. A depth-1,000 type that fits wire metadata and requires only a four-byte float payload adds approximately 167 million classification visits per decoded row. This work runs synchronously in Scan.

issues.title: vectorElemMinSize returns 1 for a 0-dim vector element, rejecting valid empty nested…
issues.verdictReason: Built a vector<vector<float,0>,2> TypeInfo and called unmarshalVector with a non-nil empty payload: it returned "unmarshal vector: 2 dimensions do not fit in 0 bytes" instead of decoding to [][]float32{}. vectorElemMinSize(vector<float,0>) returns 1 (the size<1 fallback at marshal.go:1141-1143) even though a 0-dimension fixed-element vector truly occupies 0 bytes, so the new bound at marshal.go:1000 rejects a payload the pre-PR code accepted.
issues.scopeReason: The dimension bound and vectorElemMinSize are new in this PR and directly cause the regression.

reportedAs.code-review-ad: Previously supported empty nested vectors (vector<vector<float,0>,N>) now rejected

reportedAsByRun.codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17/tidepool: marshal.go:1142 assigns a one-byte minimum to vector<float,0>, although its fixed-length encoding occupies zero bytes. For vector<vector<float,0>,2>, a non-NULL empty payload and [][]float32 destination succeed at base but fail the new outer bound, even though both pinned metadata parsers admit zero dimensions and the exported zero-dimension API remains explicitly supported by tests.

issues.verdictReason: Read the test at marshal_vector_test.go:767-786: the comment says each inner vector is "a vint length followed by three vint lengths of zero: eight bytes", but the assertion two lines later checks the combined payload for both inner vectors equals 8 bytes total, i.e. 4 bytes per inner vector, not 8.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is part of this PR's newly added test file content.

reportedAs.code-review-ad: Test comment misattributes eight bytes to each inner vector instead of four

reportedAsByRun.codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17/tidepool: marshal_vector_test.go:772's comment describes one outer length vint plus three zero-length text vints as eight bytes per inner vector, but that is actually four bytes per inner vector — eight bytes is the total for both elements. The aggregate assertion itself is correct.

issues.title: Test/helper comments wrongly claim an N-element vector is never fewer than N bytes
issues.verdictReason: The comment at marshal_vector_test.go:691-692 (and the matching vectorElemMinSize doc comment at marshal.go:1121-1124) claims a vector of N elements is never encoded in fewer than N bytes; confirmed via I2's reproduction that an outer vector of N zero-dimension inner vectors encodes to exactly 0 bytes regardless of N, contradicting the stated universal floor.
issues.scopeReason: The comment and the code whose behavior it mischaracterizes are both new in this PR.

reportedAs.code-review-ad: Documented byte minima claim wrongly excludes supported zero-byte encodings

reportedAsByRun.codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17/tidepool: marshal_vector_test.go:693 states an N-element vector never occupies fewer than N bytes, and line 813 likewise denies a zero-byte element encoding, but an outer vector containing N zero-dimensional fixed-element vectors occupies zero bytes. The helper's 'fewest bytes' description at marshal.go:1121 and the first commit's universal one-byte claim repeat this same incorrect premise.

issues.title: Zero-dim nested vector element lets dimension bound admit N up to payload length,…
issues.verdictReason: Reproduced directly: unmarshalVector on vector<vector<float,0>,N> with a 1 MiB payload and N set to the bound's allowed maximum (len(data)) allocated ~25.17 MB (measured via runtime.MemStats) before the first inner vector's nonempty-data check rejected it -- matching the predicted 24*N bytes for a [][]float32 destination on amd64. The root cause is the same vectorElemMinSize==1 floor from I2 for zero-dimension elements, which lets N scale with raw payload bytes instead of being rejected outright.
issues.scopeReason: This PR's own new bound and vectorElemMinSize logic determine the allowed N for this case; the residual amplification is a gap in the new hardening this PR added, not an unrelated pre-existing path.

reportedAs.code-review-ad: Zero-dim nested elements allocate 24N bytes before rejection, hardening gap unclosed

reportedAsByRun.codex-code-review-ad-2026-10-17/tidepool: marshal.go:1142 permits vector<vector<float,0>,N> with N equal to its nonempty payload length; decoding into [][]float32 allocates 24N bytes on amd64 before the first inner vector rejects its nonempty chunk, so a 1 MiB payload causes 24 MiB of outer slice-header allocation. This exposure predates the PR and remains unclosed by the advertised recursive hardening; the description's companion dim < 1 rejection is absent from both pinned parsers, and the new allocation test exercises inner dimension three instead.
